newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Tamil Tigers say eight Sri Lanka troops killed.
newsitem.headline: Tamil Tigers say eight Sri Lanka troops killed.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Tamil Tiger guerrillas said on Wednesday that they had killed at least eight soldiers in a midnight attack on the army's northern forward defences.
The rebels' Voice of Tigers radio broadcast said guerrillas attacked soldiers in their bunkers on Monday night and made off with a large haul of small arms and ammunition.
A Defence Ministry statement said on Wednesday that four civilian home guards and one soldier were killed in the attack in Vavuniya district, 200 km (125 miles) northeast of the capital Colombo.
Eight home guards and seven soldiers were wounded, the statement said.
The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka.
On Tuesday, at least five soldiers were killed and four wounded when their tractor was blown up by a rebel landmine in Kallar, in northeastern Trincomalee, a separate Defence Ministry statement said.
Security forces launched a new offensive on Monday against the rebels in eastern Batticaloa, about 200 km (125 miles) east of Colombo, to flush rebels from jungle camps.
The LTTE said last week that they had lost more than 9,000 members in their war for independence, now in its 14th year.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war. The rebels say the toll is much higher.
